title: The Bench I Was Too Polite to Leave
scene: You sit on a park bench with time to spare before meeting a friend. An elderly man starts chatting, and you keep waiting for a natural break in the conversation because leaving feels rude, only to discover he is perfectly comfortable when you finally say you have to go.
sceneJa: 友人との待ち合わせまで時間があり、公園のベンチで休んでいると高齢の男性に話しかけられる。帰るタイミングを逃し続けるが、いざ『行かなければ』と伝えると、相手はまったく気にしていなかった。

chunks.en: I stopped at a small park
chunks.ja: 小さな公園に立ち寄りました
帰宅途中に

chunks.en: because I had about twenty minutes to spare
chunks.ja: 20分ほど時間に余裕があったので
友人と会う前に
空いているベンチを見つけ
大きな木の下で
コーヒーを持って座り

chunks.en: and immediately felt rather pleased with the arrangement.
chunks.ja: すぐに、なかなか良い選択だったと思いました
数分後

chunks.en: an elderly man sat beside me
chunks.ja: 高齢の男性が隣に座り
そして尋ねました

chunks.en: I came to the park often.
chunks.ja: この公園によく来るのかと
『それほどでも』と答え
それが〜になると思っていました
始まりであり終わりに
私たちの会話の
ところが彼は話してくれました

chunks.en: about the pond, the local cats,
chunks.ja: 池や近所の猫について
近くにある3軒のカフェについて

chunks.en: and a surprisingly complicated dispute about some pigeons.
chunks.ja: そして鳩をめぐる意外に複雑な揉め事について
15分ほど経ったところで

chunks.en: I realised I needed to leave,
chunks.ja: そろそろ出なければならないと気づきました
しかし彼はちょうど差しかかっていました

chunks.en: what seemed to be an important part of the pigeon story.
chunks.ja: 鳩の話の重要そうな部分に
私は待ち続けました

chunks.en: for a natural break in the conversation,
chunks.ja: 会話が自然に切れる瞬間を
でも終わりそうになるたびに
新しい鳩が登場するようでした
結局

chunks.en: I apologised and said I had to go,
chunks.ja: 謝って、もう行かなければならないと言うと
彼はただ笑って

chunks.en: and said, "Of course. Have a good evening."
chunks.ja: 『もちろん。良い夜を』と言いました

chunks.en: I had spent ten extra minutes
chunks.ja: 私は10分余計に使っていました

chunks.en: worrying that leaving would seem rude,
chunks.ja: 途中で帰ったら失礼に見えるのではと心配することに
一方で彼はまったく気にしていないようでした

chunks.en: with the idea that conversations sometimes end.
chunks.ja: 会話はいずれ終わるということを
それは有益な気づきでした
社会的なプレッシャーの一部は
親切にも提供されているのだと
自分自身によって

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: I kept waiting / for a natural break in the conversation / but every possible ending / appeared to contain another pigeon
I kept / waiting for a natural / break in the conversation but / every possible ending appeared to contain another pigeon
I kept waiting for / a natural break / in the conversation but every / possible ending
questions.explanation: The first version separates the ongoing action, the thing the speaker is waiting for, and the humorous contrast that follows.

questions.question: What does ‘have time to spare’ mean?
options: Be exactly on time with no extra time
Have forgotten what time it is
questions.explanation: ‘Have time to spare’ means having extra time beyond what you need.

questions.question: What does the speaker realise at the end?
options: The man was offended when the speaker left
The pressure to stay had mostly come from the speaker's own assumptions
The pigeon story was more important than the meeting
questions.explanation: The man accepts the goodbye easily, showing that much of the awkwardness existed in the speaker’s own expectations.

speak: Start relaxed and conversational. Let the pigeon story build with mild amusement rather than irritation. Slow slightly at ‘a natural break in the conversation’. Read ‘every possible ending appeared to contain another pigeon’ very straight. In the final two sentences, sound reflective and lightly self-aware, not preachy.
review: Flow: spare time → friendly conversation → difficulty finding an exit → self-imposed politeness pressure → easy goodbye → dry realisation. Useful chunks: ‘have time to spare’, ‘a natural break in the conversation’, and ‘appear comfortable with ...’. The humour comes from discovering that the social rule causing the pressure may have existed mostly in the speaker’s own head.
